questions.q: For a Giffen good, which statement is correct?
options: It is a normal good with an upward-sloping demand
Income effect is positive and weaker than substitution effect
It is inferior and the income effect outweighs the substitution effect
questions.explanation: A Giffen good is inferior, and its (perverse) income effect is larger than the always-negative substitution effect, so demand slopes upward.

questions.q: Consumer equilibrium in indifference curve analysis requires:
options: MRSxy = Px/Py with the IC convex to the origin
questions.explanation: Tangency (MRS = price ratio) is the first-order condition; convexity of the IC is the second-order condition.

questions.q: Hicksian substitution effect keeps which of the following constant?
options: Real income measured as utility level
questions.explanation: Hicks compensates to keep the consumer on the same indifference curve (same utility). Slutsky keeps purchasing power constant.

questions.q: If price elasticity of demand is 2 and price is ₹40, marginal revenue is:
A monopolist will never operate where demand is:
questions.explanation: With ed < 1, MR is negative, but MC is positive, so MR = MC cannot hold there.

questions.q: The kinked demand curve model explains:
questions.explanation: Sweezy (1939): rivals match price cuts but not rises, giving a kink and a gap in MR, so price stays rigid.

questions.q: In the Cournot duopoly with zero costs and linear demand, total industry output is what fraction of the competitive output?
questions.explanation: Each firm produces 1/3 of the competitive output, so together 2/3.
Baumol gave sales-revenue maximisation. Monopolistic competition is Chamberlin's; revealed preference is Samuelson's; the contract curve is Edgeworth's.

questions.q: Elasticity of substitution of a Cobb–Douglas production function is:
questions.explanation: Cobb–Douglas always has σ = 1, whatever the returns to scale.

questions.q: The shutdown point of a competitive firm is at the minimum of:
questions.explanation: Below minimum AVC the firm cannot even cover variable costs, so it shuts down in the short run.

questions.q: Lerner's index of monopoly power equals:

questions.explanation: Exchange efficiency: every consumer has the same MRS between any two goods (a point on the contract curve).
Akerlof showed hidden quality information before trade (adverse selection) can make markets collapse.

questions.q: Quasi-rent is a concept given by:
questions.explanation: Marshall: short-run earnings of fixed factors over and above variable cost.

questions.q: Arrow's impossibility theorem does NOT include which condition?
questions.explanation: Arrow's conditions: unrestricted domain, Pareto, IIA, non-dictatorship (and transitivity). Lump-sum transfers are from the second welfare theorem.
